findings.description: The current_regular_contract check added in validate_ledger (line 3456) runs for ALL run records with a matching reviewer dict, not just clear runs with execution_proof. A failed regular GLM review (tool-failure, unreviewed, etc.) creates a reviewer record via append_failed_run (line 5768) that carries review_contract_sha256 (set at line 6248) and review_family_mode but never sets terminal_provider, terminal_model, review_depth_passes, or review_depth_mode. Those fields are only set on successful completion: terminal identity at lines 5327-5328, and depth fields at lines 5061-5062 (only when final_completed is True). On failure, the two-pass finally block at lines 5065-5066 explicitly pops review_depth_passes and review_depth_mode. When the ledger with this failed run is loaded on the next invocation, validate_ledger hits the require at line 3468 and rejects the entire ledger with 'current regular review contract is missing terminal or depth fields', making the ledger permanently unloadable and blocking all future crosscheck operations for that task. The fix is to gate the current_regular_contract check on execution_proof being present (or on the run state being clear), matching the pattern of the adjacent execution_proof-gated block at line 3478.

findings.title: Failed regular GLM review permanently corrupts the ledger via ungated current_regular_contract validation

runs.summary: Reviewed the full 4-file diff (516 insertions, 17 deletions) implementing a two-pass regular GLM review protocol. The PR adds an isolated challenge pass followed by an authoritative synthesis pass, with bounded untrusted hypothesis projection, aggregated telemetry, and fail-closed validation for current-contract records missing terminal or depth fields. I verified implementation correctness of combine_review_telemetry (aggregation, missing values, mixed sources, boolean rejection, empty parts), review_depth_projection (correct stripping of execution claims including executed_reproduction, reproduction, mutation_proof, and equivalent_to), and regular_review_depth_context (pass validation and prior-count enforcement). However, I found a blocking issue: the new current_regular_contract validation in validate_ledger is not gated on execution_proof or run state being clear, so it applies to ALL run records matching the current regular contract, including failed runs (tool-failure, unreviewed). A failed regular GLM review's reviewer record carries review_contract_sha256 and review_family_mode but never sets terminal_provider, terminal_model, review_depth_passes, or review_depth_mode (those are only set on successful completion at lines 5327-5328 and 5061-5062). When the ledger is loaded on the next invocation, validate_ledger rejects the failed run, making the ledger permanently unloadable and blocking all future crosscheck operations for that task.

Pass 2 (authoritative synthesis) review of PR #330 — fix(crosscheck): add two-pass regular review evidence. The diff spans 4 files (bin/fm-crosscheck.py, tests/fm-crosscheck.test.sh, docs/azure-requirements.md, docs/crosscheck.md) with 562 insertions and 17 deletions. I independently inspected the complete full diff and executed focused Python-level reproductions for every concrete concern.

Key implementation areas verified:

1. Two-pass protocol (run_reviewer, lines ~4966-5066): The challenge pass creates a fresh git checkout (challenge_dir), deep-copies config, sets _review_depth_pass="challenge", and calls run_reviewer recursively. The recursive call skips the two-pass trigger (since _review_depth_pass is not None) and falls through to normal Pi review logic. After the challenge succeeds, its verdict is projected via review_depth_projection (bounded string clipping, max 8 findings/suspicions/updates, max 12 citations each). The synthesis pass runs in the original review_dir with _review_depth_pass="final" and receives the projection as prior analysis. The finally block combines telemetry, sums turn counts, and sets depth fields only if the synthesis completed.

2. Validation (validate_ledger, lines ~3456-3551): A "current_regular_contract" check identifies reviews matching the regular GLM lane, cross-family primary mode, non-Azure execution, and current review contract hash. For clear/blocking states, all four terminal/depth fields are required. Inside the execution_proof block, terminal fields are validated against the expected provider/model, and depth fields are validated against the fixed constants. The turn_count >= depth_passes check ensures every pass contributed at least one turn. I verified via direct Python tests that: (a) valid clear records with all fields pass, (b) clear records missing any of the 4 fields are rejected, (c) blocking records missing fields are rejected, (d) tool-failure, unreviewed, and cannot-certify records without depth fields remain reloadable, (e) wrong terminal_provider is rejected, (f) wrong review_depth_mode is rejected, (g) turn_count < depth_passes is rejected.

3. Projection safety (review_depth_projection, lines ~4207-4296): I verified that the projection strips reproduction, mutation_proof, and equivalent_to fields from findings and finding_updates, preventing execution claims from leaking into the synthesis prompt. Only title, severity, description, citations (for findings), description, citations (for suspicions), and id, status, note (for updates) are projected.

4. Telemetry combination (combine_review_telemetry, lines ~4897-4960): I verified that integer and float values are correctly summed across passes, None values propagate (sum becomes None), mismatched source strings yield "mixed-or-unavailable-pass-sources", and an empty parts list raises CrosscheckError.

5. Terminal identity (pi_review_result, lines ~4885-4895; run_reviewer, lines ~5327-5328): The terminal_identity dict is populated only after pi_review_result validates provider/model match. Since expected_provider and expected_model are non-None strings and the function calls tool_fail if they don't match, both keys are guaranteed present when the function returns normally. The direct dict access at lines 5327-5328 is safe.

6. Failed record lifecycle: Challenge pass failure propagates telemetry but not turn count or terminal/depth fields to config, so failed records remain correctly shaped. Synthesis pass failure pops depth fields in the finally block. Internal _review_depth_pass and _review_depth_prior keys are always cleaned from config before returning or raising.

7. Tests: The PR adds test_current_regular_contract_requires_reuse_evidence (verifies removing any of 4 fields blocks reuse) and test_failed_current_regular_contract_remains_reloadable (verifies failed-then-successful retry works). The existing test_telemetry_economics_and_exact_head_reuse was updated to reflect doubled telemetry (2 passes). I could not run the full bash test suite due to sandbox admission restrictions, but I verified all implementation logic through direct Python imports and assertions.

Existing finding cc-6f8469a6098b (blocking, opened at head fbdcfc97881dfb5b707c1675772e455449b47690) remains open: that head is not present in this repository's history, so I cannot inspect the code at that point or determine whether this PR's changes address it.
